cards.title: From crumpled paper to on-time doses
cards.body: A prescription only helps if the right tablet is taken at the right time. Here's how AICA is designed to turn paper into reminders.

cards.title: Step 1: snap the prescription
cards.body: The patient or a family member takes a clear photo of the paper prescription inside AICA.

cards.title: Step 2: AI reads the handwriting
cards.body: AI picks out medicine names, doses and timings from the photo. Doctor handwriting is hard, so this reading is never treated as final.

cards.title: Step 3: you confirm against the photo
cards.body: You check what AI read side by side with the original photo and fix anything wrong. Nothing is saved until you confirm.

cards.title: Step 4: reminders get set
cards.body: Confirmed timings become dose reminders, including Indian patterns like 1-0-1 and half tablets. Each family profile gets its own.

cards.title: Step 5: one thread for what's next
cards.body: The prescription sits on a shared thread with the chemist and doctor, so refills and the next visit start from the same record.

cards.title: Built carefully, still early
cards.body: AICA is at early MVP stage, with pilots starting in Lucknow. Try the interactive prototype and join the waitlist at aicaglobal.in.

takeaway: Snap, AI reads, you confirm against the photo, then reminders are set. Nothing is saved until a person checks it.
share: AICA turns a paper prescription into dose reminders, and you confirm every line first. aicaglobal.in
